summary.headline: JK Tyre Q1FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell to Rs.268 crore (6.8% margin) from Rs.424 crore, as raw material costs rose ~20% QoQ.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 2% YoY to Rs.3,956 crore, while EBITDA dropped about 37% YoY to Rs.268 crore and PAT was Rs.43 crore. India domestic volumes grew 25% YoY, led by 42% OEM growth, but India revenue growth was about 14%, implying weaker realisations. Mexico (JK Tornel) was hit by input shortages and a productivity-related slowdown, and net debt rose Rs.500 crore QoQ to Rs.4,945 crore. Management guided to margin recovery from the second half, with 10-11% FY27 operating margins as the working assumption.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity / Net debt to EBITDA

segments.name: India domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic volumes grew 25% YoY across replacement and OE; OEM volumes grew 42%, TBR OE +18% and TBR replacement +15%. Net sales realisation rose about 5% QoQ and about 4% YoY on a standalone basis.

segments.name: Passenger lines (PCR)
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 10% YoY, led by OEM. Sixteen-inch and above rim sizes make up 35% of PCR sales volume.

segments.name: Farm
segments.commentary: Volumes grew 31% YoY, with OEM +35% and replacement +25%.

segments.name: 2/3-wheeler
segments.commentary: OE volumes grew 17% and replacement volumes grew 48% YoY.

segments.name: JK Tornel (Mexico)
segments.commentary: Output was constrained by input shortages (bead wire largely from China, shipping disruption) and a productivity-negotiation slowdown, since resolved. An analyst cited a decline of about 82%, which management did not dispute.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth expected at good double digits (about 10-11%), driven by price hikes and volume, with new capacity running fully by Q3 FY27.
FY27 operating margin guided at about 10-11%, which management said may be below FY26; margins expected to improve progressively from H2 FY27, returning to 11-13%.
Further price increases of 8-9% planned; cumulative increase of about 11% taken in the replacement market to date.
Raw material costs expected to rise a further 8-10% in Q2 from higher-cost inventory, then stabilise; natural rubber expected to stay range-bound after some softening.
Total debt expected to rise by Rs.500-700 crore in FY27 to fund capex and working capital.
Mexico expected to deliver better results than Q1 in the remaining three quarters.
capex_capacity: Expansion plan worth Rs.4,980 crore for PCR and TBR at the Chennai tyre plant (about 24% capacity addition over roughly four years, per management).
Capacity additions in the next financial year to be mainly TBR and passenger car, plus balancing at Banmore; expected to add about 7% to current installed capacity.
Indian capacity utilisation about 95%; consolidated utilisation about 80%. TBR and 2/3W near full; PCR about 95%; LCV and farm above 95%.
Upgradation and modernisation project under way at JK Tornel, Mexico.
demand_pricing: Indian auto retail sales grew more than 15% (FADA source); PV +23%, CV +14%, 2/3W +14%, farm +22%.
Price hike of about 5% taken in Q1, applied in monthly staggered steps; 8-9% more planned, with OEM price increases flowing with a lag.
Natural rubber (RSS4) prices softening in India; management hopes for a fall by next quarter.
Export volumes from India rose 2% QoQ.
Product mix at consolidated level: truck and bus 56%, passenger line radial 27%, 2/3W 5%, others 12%.

qa_highlights.question: Vijay Kumar (Axis Capital): India volume growth of 25% versus India revenue growth of about 14%; does this imply lower pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said domestic volumes grew 25% YoY; net effective price increase was about 4% YoY on a standalone basis and NSR rose about 5% QoQ. OEM prices lag, so the full effect will show in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Vijay Kumar: What drove the Mexico weakness, and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Dr. Bajoria cited constrained inputs (bead wire from China, shipping disruption, container shortages, NR up about 18%) and productivity negotiations with workers; these are resolved and management expects better results in the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Bhagnani (Living Root Analytics): What margin and revenue trajectory for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins to improve progressively from H2 FY27 once raw material costs stabilise; price hikes should cover the RM increase except 1-2%. FY27 revenue growth guided at about 10-11%; operating margin about 10-11%.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Bhagnani: Will debt rise this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, net debt is expected to rise by Rs.500-700 crore in FY27 due to capex disbursements and working capital, partly offset by repayments and internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Krish Jain (NAFA): What capacity utilisation and additions are planned?
qa_highlights.answer: India utilisation about 95%, consolidated about 80%. Capacity additions of about 7% by next financial year, mainly TBR and PCR, with the full run-rate expected by Q3 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Digant Shah (DAM Capital): Will Mexico production normalise to Q3/Q4 revenue levels? What is the USMCA status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the record: it was a slowdown, not a strike. Production has resumed and is near normal, with similar topline expected. USMCA has been renewed for 10 years.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on RM cost stabilisation after a further 8-10% increase expected in Q2 FY27 from high-cost inventory.
Mexico output recovery and the sustainability of the bead wire supply from China amid US-China tensions.
Net debt rising to about Rs.5,400-5,600 crore by year-end (Rs.500-700 crore increase) with net debt/EBITDA at 2.56x in Q1, against a margin recovery that is not yet visible.
Price hike realisation (8-9% planned) versus volume response, with OEM price lags.
EV tyre replacement life: management cited about 5-10% shorter life due to higher torque, with the degree depending on usage.
key_quotes: And I can only assure you that this year, in the remaining 3 quarters, we will be definitely showing you better results than in Q1.

Mr. Vijay, as I said that during this quarter, the operations at Tornel, Mexico were impacted due to the ongoing geopolitical disruptions resulting in constrained availability of key inputs, which also affected the output.
Thank you. First of all, I want to make a small correction that it was not a strike, it was a slowdown.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on demand and the medium-term outlook, citing record industry growth and 25% domestic volume growth. It was cautious on near-term margins, guiding only to a 10-11% FY27 operating margin "if I have to make a guess" and avoiding a firm Mexico recovery figure. Answers on Mexico were defensive, with the CEO-level speaker correcting the "strike" framing and asserting normalisation without quantifying it.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 10-11% on 8-9% further price hikes plus volume, with margins of 10-11% for FY27 recovering to 11-13% in H2; capacity is backed by the approved Rs.4,980 crore Chennai expansion (~24%, four years out) and ~7% Banmore/TBR additions next FY, but the near-term volume lift relies on existing ~95% India utilisation and pricing rather than dated
